attackVerdicts.attack: designBreak-1: a source-path launch (bun run src/..., brain shim) from an untrusted cwd still gets Bun's .env/.env.local autoload, so R1 Option 1 does not close SEC-1/QUANTA_PERMISSION/QUANTA_API_KEY_HELPER on that path
attackVerdicts.evidence: Probe S1/S2 (bun 1.3.14, evil cwd): `bun file` and `bun run file` both printed EVIL_PRELOAD_RAN and ENTRY {DOTENV_X, DOTENV_LOCAL_X, DOTENV_DEVELOPMENT_X}. Real CLI one-shot (`bun <repo>/src/apps/cli/index.ts "say hi"`) from a cwd whose `.env` carried QUANTA_API_KEY_HELPER + OPENAI_BASE_URL: pwned=true, listener got 45x POST /v1/chat/completions `Bearer sk-minted` + 6x /v1/embeddings `Bearer sk-probe-REALENV-openai`. Scope caveat (measured): package.json scripts run with cwd = package root (`bun run x` from pkg/sub printed pkg), so the dev scripts never launch from a foreign cwd. Quanta-authored launchers with an uncontrolled cwd are the terminal shim (quanta-terminal-brain:83) and the side-agent fork (side-agent-fork-port.ts:228, cwd=cfg.cwd per agent-config-assembler.ts:487).

attackVerdicts.attack: designBreak-2: a cwd bunfig.toml preload runs on the source path, and no bun runtime flag suppresses it
attackVerdicts.verdict: CONFIRMED (mechanism); the 'no flag suppresses it' part is REFUTED
attackVerdicts.evidence: The preload does run on source: S1/S2 printed EVIL_PRELOAD_RAN, and S3 `--no-env-file` still ran it (only dotenv was suppressed). But `--config=/dev/null` does suppress it: S11 showed no preload (dotenv still loaded), S6/S12 `--no-env-file --config=/dev/null` gave ENTRY {} with no preload, and child_process.fork with execArgv ["--no-env-file","--config=/dev/null"] and cwd=evil gave ENTRY {} with no preload (the default fork printed EVIL_PRELOAD_RAN). `-c <path>` with a space is not a working form; use `--config=`. Parent directories are not walked (S8 subdir: nothing loaded). Whether Harbor's host cwd can be attacker-controlled is still unmeasured.

attackVerdicts.attack: missedHole-1: QUANTA_API_KEY_HELPER from launch-cwd dotenv = arbitrary command execution, bypassing the SESSION_FORBIDDEN hardening of QUANTA_LLM_CREDENTIAL_TRUSTED
attackVerdicts.verdict: CONFIRMED for Bun-autoloaded .env/.env.local; REFUTED for .env.dev through the real entrypoints
attackVerdicts.evidence: Real CLI from source with cwd .env: pwned=true. HEAD-built binary without the flags, same .env: pwned=true and chat carried `Bearer sk-minted`. A getter trap on process.env.QUANTA_API_KEY_HELPER shows why: the first read happens at logger.ts:78 -> resolveLevel (logger.ts:9) -> runtimeConfig() (runtime-config.ts:805), which caches, and only afterwards does TRAP_SET fire from env-files.ts:49 via cli/index.ts:33. So runtimeConfig-read knobs set by quanta's loader are inert by accident. The attacker's direct buildLLMWithByok call skipped that cache. QUANTA_LLM_CREDENTIAL_TRUSTED is in SESSION_FORBIDDEN_KNOBS (knob-overrides.ts:31).

revisedDesign.summary: Close both launch-cwd channels with exact rules, no trust prompt and no key classification. (1) Every quanta-controlled Bun invocation disables Bun's cwd autoload: shipped compiled artifacts get --no-compile-autoload-dotenv --no-compile-autoload-bunfig, and quanta-authored bun launchers with an uncontrolled cwd (side-agent fork, terminal-bench shim) get --no-env-file --config=/dev/null. All flags are measured on Bun 1.3.14. (2) Quanta's one dotenv loader resolves its directory only from the running code's own checkout root. It loads .env.dev/.env.local/.env only when realpath(launch cwd) === realpath(checkout root), and never inside a compiled binary. The bench duplicate parser is deleted. (3) An AST census makes a new unhardened compile site, a new bun fork launcher, a sixth dotenv reader, or an argument-injected loader call a red build.
revisedDesign.structuralMechanism: Same-owner identity replaces trust inference. The only directory that may feed quanta's process env from launch-time files is the directory holding the code being executed, because anyone who can write its .env.dev can already edit src/. The loader's single exported entry `loadLaunchDotenv()` computes a closed discriminated resolution `{kind: 'checkout-root'} | {kind: 'not-checkout-root'} | {kind: 'compiled-binary'} | {kind: 'cwd-unresolvable'}` from import.meta.url (Bun realpaths module URLs — measured with a symlinked tree) and realpath(process.cwd()). Only 'checkout-root' reaches the private loadOne. 'compiled-binary' is decided explicitly from the `/$bunfs/` marker, which is required because resolve('/$bunfs/root','..','..') === '/' (measured) would otherwise equal a '/' launch cwd. The raw `loadEnvFiles(files)` export is removed, so a stale caller fails at module link time. There are two SSOTs for Bun flag facts, each with its own consumers: tools/bin/compile-flags.ts `BUN_COMPILE_NO_CWD_AUTOLOAD_FLAGS` for build tooling, and src/shared/bun-runtime.ts `BUN_RUNTIME_NO_CWD_AUTOLOAD_ARGV` plus `isCompiledSingleFileBinaryUrl`, hoisted from side-agent-fork-port.ts:86-97. A pure AST detector (tools/dev/launch-cwd-autoload-census.ts, closed-union finding kinds with an exhaustive Record and a runtime drift guard) and a closed JSON manifest enforce every site.

revisedDesign.compatibilityAndMigration: Byte-identical in three cases. (1) Every package.json script: `bun run <script>` executes with cwd = package root, measured from a subdir, so cwd === checkout root. (2) In-process tests: bun test runs from the repo root. (3) Scratch-cwd subprocess tests, which already avoided the repo .env.dev on purpose. The remote bench runs `~/.bun/bin/bun run src/apps/bench/cli.ts` with a relative path (box-session.ts:408), i.e. from the repo root, so it is also unchanged. Intended behaviour changes: compiled binaries (the installed quanta and a rebuilt web daemon) never load any launch-cwd dotenv or bunfig; source launches from a non-root cwd no longer load that cwd's .env.dev/.env.local/.env through quanta's loader; the side-agent worker and brain shim children ignore their cwd's bunfig/.env. The tracked daemon binaries stay vulnerable until rebuilt (user decision). Developers who run the INSTALLED binary inside the quanta repo and rely on .env.dev for keys must export them or use /login (user decision).
revisedDesign.userVisibleBehavior: The installed `quanta` and the desktop daemon (after rebuild) no longer execute a bunfig.toml preload or read any .env* from the directory they are launched in. `bun run dev/start/agent/eval/bench` from the quanta checkout behaves as today. Running quanta source from any other directory no longer loads that directory's .env* through quanta. There is no new prompt and no new knob. An optional one-line CLI notice when the launch cwd has LAUNCH_DOTENV_FILES that were not loaded is left to user decision D4.
revisedDesign.rollout: Default-ON and unconditional, with no gate. This is a security boundary: a knob would itself be settable from a Bun-autoloaded .env on the source path, and a default-OFF gate would ship the hole. The escape hatch for developers is launching from the checkout root or exporting real env.

userDecisions.question: D1: Which rule decides whether a launch directory's .env.dev/.env.local/.env may enter the quanta process?
userDecisions.options: (a) Checkout-root identity: load only when realpath(cwd) === the running code's checkout root; compiled binaries never load. Synchronous, no trust input, no prompt, identical for package scripts and tests. (b) R1 trust-store gate: async TrustStore plus QUANTA_TRUSTED_PATHS; needs new CLI trust wiring and a prompt; keeps installed-binary .env.dev once the repo is trusted. (c) Drop the loader entirely: dev scripts switch to Bun's native --env-file (measured later-file-wins, missing file silently ignored, real env wins; its parser differs from quanta's) and ADR-0555 provenance is retired.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a). It is the smallest change that removes the channel, a strict subset of today's behaviour, and needs no bootstrap-trust ordering. (b) can be layered on later for compiled binaries without undoing (a).

userDecisions.question: D2: Accept that the INSTALLED binary run inside the quanta repo stops reading .env.dev (keys and knobs)?
userDecisions.options: Accept (keys come from real env or /login; the Bash tool shell exported no provider keys, and ~/.quanta/auth holds chatgpt accounts) vs. add an operator channel for compiled binaries later (trust-store gate, or an absolute QUANTA_ENV_FILE read from real env).
userDecisions.recommendation: Accept now and revisit only if it causes friction. Any operator channel must never be cwd-relative.

userDecisions.question: D3: The tracked apps/tauri-shell/binaries/quanta-web-daemon* (commit 60300c637, 2026-05-27) stay exploitable until rebuilt. Rebuild and commit, or untrack?
userDecisions.options: Rebuild via prepare-build.sh after C1 (needs the Tauri/Swift toolchain) vs. stop tracking prebuilt binaries.
userDecisions.recommendation: Rebuild right after C1 lands. Tracked binaries will drift from the source flags again, so consider untracking as a follow-up.

userDecisions.question: D4: Print a notice when the launch cwd holds LAUNCH_DOTENV_FILES that were not loaded?
userDecisions.options: No notice (silent) vs. one logger.warn in the CLI entry only, naming the files and how to supply keys (existence check only, no values read).
userDecisions.recommendation: One CLI-only warn, as a transitional aid for D2 users.

userDecisions.question: D5: Fix the separate correctness bug that runtimeConfig() is cached at logger.ts:78 before any dotenv load, so runtimeConfig-read knobs from .env.dev are inert while direct process.env reads are not?
userDecisions.options: Out of scope (follow-up that moves the loader into a pre-import bootstrap entry) vs. fold into C3b.
userDecisions.recommendation: Separate follow-up. Folding it in would change which developer .env.dev knobs take effect, which is a behaviour change unrelated to the security boundary.

userDecisions.question: D6: Stop the model from writing workspace bunfig.toml/.env*/package.json, matching Claude Code's denyWrite (chunk-bdzrjgqf.js:1520)?
userDecisions.options: Separate cluster vs. extend src/permission/git-write-guard.ts now.
userDecisions.recommendation: Separate cluster. After C1-C3 quanta itself no longer autoloads them, but any later `bun` in that workspace would.

residualRisks: A human launching quanta source by hand (`bun /path/to/quanta/src/...`) from a hostile cwd is still exposed to Bun's own bunfig preload and .env/.env.local autoload before any quanta code runs. Nothing in-process can undo that (measured S1 ordering). It is bounded to developer/manual use: package scripts pin cwd to the package root (measured), and quanta-authored launchers are hardened in C2.

Bun version drift: the flag names and defaults, `--config=/dev/null` semantics, realpath'd module URLs and the `/$bunfs/` marker were measured only on Bun 1.3.14 (Claude Code's binary is 1.4.1). T1/T6/T7 re-measure behaviourally with paired controls on every run, so drift shows up as red rather than a silent pass.
Real-env BUN_OPTIONS is still honored by a hardened compiled binary (measured: `BUN_OPTIONS=--preload` injected). That is operator-controlled env, not a launch-cwd channel.
runtimeConfig is cached before the loader (logger.ts:78, D5), so .env.dev knobs read through runtimeConfig are inert for developers while direct process.env reads are live.
The ADR-0555 provenance registry stays blind to .env/.env.local that Bun autoloads from the developer's own checkout root on the source path. After the fix this affects consent UX only.

Unmeasured: HTTPS-proxy MITM without CA injection, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, QUANTA_SANDBOX / QUANTA_TRUSTED_PATHS / QUANTA_CENTRAL_CONFIG end-to-end, and QUANTA_LLM_REPLAY (only R1 measured it). All are closed wholesale by C1+C3b because the design classifies no keys.
Unmeasured: the terminal-bench host cwd under Harbor, the Tauri sidecar's actual cwd, and whether the non-interactive default posture denies a replayed `write` (T4 must measure this in its RED step).
Unmeasured: whether an unused-export or dead-code ratchet objects to tools/bin/compile-flags.ts or src/shared/bun-runtime.ts exports consumed only by tools/tests; check during C1/C2.
The committed Tauri daemon binaries stay vulnerable until D3 is done.
tools/leaderboard-dashboard/server.ts:1080 and tools/dev/mutation-check.ts:390 spawn `bun` from dev tooling. They were not classified by the census because they are not production launchers.
readiness: READY-WITH-DECISIONS. C1 (compile flags + census) and C2 (fork/shim runtime argv) can start now; both are measured to close their channels and are small, independently green commits. C3a/C3b wait only on D1 (loader rule). Checkout-root identity is recommended because its RED proofs are measured, it adds no trust input or prompt, and it is byte-identical for scripts and tests. D2-D6 are non-blocking.
